exact_replacement.new_text:
Use at most n_K pieces, with n_K depending only on K,T,θ and uniformly bounded for every start s. Index the pieces by j=1,...,n, where n≤n_K. The identity initial operator has norm1. Before piece j, the second evolution has norm at most2^(j−1), so its local path norm on that piece satisfies Nℓ(V′)≤2^j. Define E_0=0 and let E_j be the difference at the RIGHT endpoint of piece j. Put a_K=cθ ℓ^θ δ. The local difference estimate gives

    E_j≤2E_(j−1)+2^(j+1)a_K,
    E_j/2^j≤E_(j−1)/2^(j−1)+2a_K≤2j a_K,
    E_j≤j 2^(j+1)cθ ℓ^θ δ.

On piece j the same recurrence bounds its full local difference norm, so the bound also controls interior times. A shorter final piece only reduces its Young coefficient. For n≤n_K, a sufficient finite global Lipschitz constant is (n_K+1)2^(n_K+2)cθ ℓ^θ, which harmlessly enlarges n_K 2^(n_K+1)cθ ℓ^θ. Hence
